newsitem.title: GREECE: GREEK BUDGET DEFICIT/GDP GOAL TO BE MET IN 97 - MIN.
newsitem.headline: GREEK BUDGET DEFICIT/GDP GOAL TO BE MET IN 97 - MIN.

text.p: Greece's general government budget deficit to GDP target of 4.2 percent will be attained in 1997 despite a shortfall in revenues that will be offset by lower expenditures, said National Economy Minister Yannos Papandoniou.

"The latest available figures show that the 4.2 percent of GDP budget deficit target will be attained despite a likely, small shortfall in revenues that will be fully offset by harnessing expenditures and especially interest payments," said Papandoniou.
The general government budget deficit stood at 7.4 percent of GDP in 1996.

Central government budget revenues rose 11.8 percent year-on-year in the first five months of 1997 and will accelerate in the next few months when the state collects the bulk of its revenues from taxes and other sources, he said.

The faster than projected easing of interest rates and the succesful introduction of long-term fixed coupon bonds that will extend the average maturity of public debt will save the budget 160 billion drachmas, added Papandoniou.
GDP growth will accelerate to 3.5 percent in 1997 from 2.6 percent in 1996 on the back of bouyant investment spending, he said.
Disbursements from the public investment programme rose 107 percent year-on-year in the first five months of this year, said Papandoniou.
The faster GDP growth and investments will reduce unemployment to 10.1 percent in 1997 from 10.4 percent in 1996, he added.

The national economy minister reiterated that average inflation would fall to about 6.0 percent in 1997, down from 8.5 percent in 1997 thanks to the government's anti-inflationary economic policy, the stricter incomes policy and the expected deceleration in import prices, he said.
The current account deficit will stand at 3.5 of GDP in 1997 from 3.8 percent last year and will be easily financed by capital inflows, said Papandoniou.
